5. Chapter on the Rainy Season Retreat (Varṣā). Section Five: The Threefold Vinaya, Chapter on the Rainy Season Retreat. The *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya* states:
There are five types of those who uphold the Vinaya.
First, those who recite from the introduction of the Prātimokṣa up to the thirty rules.
This was the first to uphold the Vinaya;
the second recited the Prātimokṣa up to the ninety rules;
and the third extensively expounded the Mahāsāṃghika Bhikṣu-prātimokṣa-sūtra.
The fourth is the extensive recitation of the two divisions of the Vinaya;
the fifth is the recitation of the entire Vinaya.
Among these, during the spring and winter, one should reside in dependence upon four types of Vinaya masters.
One must not rely on the *duṣkṛta* [offense].
During the summer retreat (*varṣā*), one should abide by the fifth rule;
if one does not so abide, one incurs a *pāyattika* offense. The *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya* states:
There are two types of *varṣā* (the rainy season retreat):
first, the early *varṣā*;
second, the late *varṣā*.
The sixteenth day of the fourth month is called the commencement of the *varṣā* (the rainy season retreat);
this is known as the "later" (*paścima*) *varṣā*. Any period other than these two is called the "intermediate" (*antarā*) *varṣā* period.
At that time, one should announce it to the person upon whom one relies.
I, [Name], am in the [Name] assembly, at the [Name] monastery,
before the [Name] dwelling.
The summer retreat is for three months;
it is for the purpose of repairing dilapidated dwellings.
Thus he spoke three times.
Those who observe the earlier *varṣā* (rainy-season retreat) perform the *pravāraṇā* on the fifteenth day of the seventh month;
those who observe the later *varṣā* perform the *pravāraṇā* on the fifteenth day of the eighth month.
In a year with an intercalary fourth month, the earlier *varṣā* period reaches its full one hundred and twenty days.
In a year with an intercalary fifth month, those who observe the later retreat complete their one hundred and twenty days;
in a year with an intercalary seventh month, those who observe the later retreat complete their one hundred and twenty days. The *Daśabhāṇavāra-vinaya* states:

Because the matters concerning the Triple Gem are of great importance, one may receive [the precepts];

this person’s violation of the summer retreat (varṣā) is equivalent in meaning to [the formal offense].

6. Chapter on the *Pravāraṇā* (Self-Indulgence), Part Six of the Threefold Vinaya; the four directions are clearly defined.
Those who entered the *pūrvavārṣika* (early rains retreat) should perform the *pravāraṇā* on the fifteenth day of the seventh month;
those who entered the *aparavārṣika* (later rains retreat) should perform the *pravāraṇā* on the fifteenth day of the eighth month;
and those who entered the intermediate retreat should depart two days after the *pravāraṇā* of the later retreaters has concluded.
The bhikṣus perform the *pravāraṇā* on the fourteenth day;
the bhikṣuṇīs perform the *pravāraṇā* on the fifteenth day.
A group of five persons should perform the *pravāraṇā* in detail.

when there is but one person, it is performed through mental reflection (*manasikāra*).

what has been seen, heard, or suspected.
